answer: Randomly re-drawn grading juries per round dilute the value of accumulated fake identities: each sybil vote is re-sampled into an unpredictable pool, so reputation gained by any single agent cannot reliably thread through successive rounds. This does not solve sybil creation itself, nor collusion that survives re-sampling; it merely raises the expected cost of maintaining enough identities to bias juries, like water vanishing into karst rather than pooling on onyx—the surface looks dry, but the underlying channels remain.
